title: Wind, Rain, Wildfire Smoke and Ash Response Planning

content.overview: Outdoor crops face events that cannot be controlled like a room setpoint. Response planning should prioritize human safety, structural/crop protection where lawful and practical, documentation, and post-event evaluation rather than improvised exposure during hazardous conditions.

vocabulary.definition: Bending or structural failure of stems from wind, crop weight or weather.
Settling of fire-generated particulate material on crop surfaces.
Predefined actions and priorities for a foreseeable disruptive event.

sections.title: Wind and rain can create structural and disease pressure
sections.body: Support, drainage, canopy density and harvest timing influence how plants respond to storms; post-event scouting should look for breakage, standing moisture and disease conditions.

sections.title: Wildfire effects extend beyond direct flame
sections.body: A 2025 survey of California cannabis producers reported reduced light, ash deposition, quality impacts, disruptions and health/safety effects associated with wildfire and smoke.

sections.title: Human safety is the primary gate
sections.body: Do not enter unsafe smoke, fire, wind or evacuation conditions merely to maintain crop operations. Crop response begins within the boundaries of emergency instructions and safe access.

workedExamples: A smoke event can reduce sunlight and deposit ash even when the farm is far from active flame.
After heavy rain, interior-canopy moisture and damaged branches deserve focused scouting rather than only checking soil moisture.
commonMistakes: Treating smoke only as a visibility issue.
Entering an unsafe evacuation area for routine crop work.
Failing to document affected lots and exposure timing.
content.practicalApplication: Create a severe-weather checklist with safety authority, crop supports/drainage, backup irrigation/power considerations, exposure records and post-event inspection/quality review.
content.summary: Outdoor resilience combines life safety, preparation, crop inspection and traceable post-event decisions.
